summary: Four surfaces, one commit each: Charts/README.md became the new repo's manual (library chart and how a consumer takes it, the publish procedure and why a published version is immutable, how a push reaches charts.home, what each gate proves); Ansible CLAUDE.md's related-repos list gained Charts and JenkinsPipelineUtils; HelmCharts CLAUDE.md now says charts/shared/_helpers.tpl has a prefixed twin in Charts that an edit here does not reach; AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/design.md names the chart homelab-shared, pins the repository URL and prefix, and corrects the hook Job skeleton, whose image line read the estate-wide pin at .Values.hook.imageTag when a library dependency's values coalesce under its own name. No change to /work/AnsibleSpecs/decisions.md (the slice changed no standing rule — the homelab doctrine file mentions chart publishing nowhere) and none to docs/runbooks/ (the one recurring procedure the slice created, publishing a version, is repo work and lives in the Charts README). Gates: kc project lint green in /work/Ansible; kc project lint and test green in /work/Charts. Architecture nudge: HelmCharts gained a chart, charts/charts, deliberately without architecture.yaml per that repo's standing instruction — the update-architecture-generated agent owes it an entry (a new in-house product serving https://charts.home in namespace charts-prd). The Ansible producer's model is untouched: no managed host, daemon or external identity changed. Handoff: the doc commits in /work/Charts and /work/HelmCharts are local and unpushed — both pushes are operator keystrokes (a Charts push rebuilds and redeploys the image; a HelmCharts push deploys straight to prd).
